coordinates.locator: OSM building footprint centroid, Hadron Experimental Facility
coordinates.note: Centroid of the Hadron Experimental Facility building footprint as traced in OpenStreetMap. It is shown as approximate because an OpenStreetMap tracing is not a surveyed detector position. It replaces the J-PARC campus-wide geocoder point, 1.66 km away.

name: Hadron Experimental Facility, J-PARC
notes: No official source consulted gives surveyed coordinates for the Hadron Experimental Facility: the fetched excerpt of the j-parc.jp Hadron Facility overview page had no location text beyond a floor-plan image. The point recorded is the centroid of the facility's building footprint as traced in OpenStreetMap (see the coordinate note).

summary.plain: The building at the J-PARC laboratory in Japan where COMET (and other experiments) search for a muon turning directly into an electron, using an intense beam of muons from J-PARC's 50 GeV proton synchrotron.
summary.technical: Hadron Experimental Facility (Hadron Hall) at J-PARC, Tokai-mura, Ibaraki, fed by the 50 GeV Main Ring slow-extracted beam; hosts COMET Phase-I among other hadron/kaon experiments. No official building-specific coordinate was found; the recorded point is the centroid of the building footprint as traced in OpenStreetMap, shown as approximate.
